title: strength_json
description: Sourced strength figures for one claim, stored as a JSON object in the strength_json column of data/claims/*/*.csv (blank when no source gives figures). Enumerations mirror schema/vocabularies.json (strength_json_basis, strength_json_vehicle_count_type, strength_json_scope, strength_json_status). For a naval claim the object may instead (or also) carry capabilities with basis refit. For an air claim it may carry aircraft (on hand, serviceable, by type of data/aircraft_types.csv), with basis reported_actual for a return and authorized_organization for an establishment.

basis.description: What kind of figure it is (vocabulary strength_json_basis).

as_of.description: Date the figure applies to (YYYY-MM-DD); may differ from the row date.

vehicles.description: Controlled snake_case vehicle type -> count. Guns are not vehicles. Adding a new typed key is a schema MINOR.

panzer_iv.description: Typed Panzer IV count; not folded into tanks.

panther.description: Typed Panther count; not folded into tanks.

tanks_and_assault_guns.description: Combined tanks and assault guns when the source does not split them (for example Panzer Lehr's 237 on 6 June 1944).

vehicle_count_type.description: What the vehicle counts mean; required with vehicles, not allowed without.

scope.description: What part of the unit the figures cover; required with personnel.

status.description: Qualitative strength a source states; destroyed is not allowed (derived from the destroyed flag).

source.description: Readable citation; must resolve through data/references_meta.csv.

value.description: The figure as the source states it, including its qualifier (for example '27,000 long tons (standard)').

unit.description: Unit of the figure where the value is a bare number, otherwise blank or absent.

reference_id.description: The reference (data/references_meta.csv) that gives this figure.

note.description: Optional: sub-type, variant, or as-built versus as-designed remark.

capabilities.description: Refit override of a ship's class capabilities (basis refit): the figures that differ from the class row of data/ship_classes.csv as of as_of, each with its own reference_id. A ship claim records a refit this way; no personnel, vehicles or status is needed. See docs/air_naval_pilot.md section 6.5.

aircraft.description: Aircraft of an air unit on the as_of date (Luftwaffe Quartermaster-General returns, USAAF unit strength reports). on_hand: aircraft held (Iststaerke, assigned or possessed); serviceable: ready for operations (einsatzbereit, operational or in commission); by_type: the same by aircraft type, an object keyed by a type_id AT### of data/aircraft_types.csv (the family row when the source gives no variant), each value {on_hand, serviceable}. A source's own figures only; unlisted types are allowed, so by_type counts may add up to less than the totals but not to more. Needs scope (what part of the unit the figures cover). Cross-checks (serviceable <= on_hand, type ids exist, domain air) are in scripts/validate.py check_aircraft_strength.

by_type.description: type_id AT### -> {on_hand, serviceable}; the keys are checked against data/aircraft_types.csv by scripts/validate.py.

examples.note: division reported 85 tanks operational on 16 June

examples.source: example only (placeholder figures and type id; real rows carry the return's own figures)
